claim: Nature (2026-10-14) reports a tetravalent nanobody IL-10R agonist designed for myeloid-selective signalling via receptor geometry/TYK2 dependence. Humanized mouse models showed anti-inflammatory effects; a humanized construct had ~8-day terminal half-life and >3-week TNF suppression after one dose in cynomolgus monkeys. Preclinical only.
falsifier: Independent human-donor assays or repeat NHP studies show material T-cell activation or hematologic toxicity at myeloid-suppressive exposure.
firstUnsupportedArrow: Preclinical cell selectivity and animal tolerability -> safe, effective durable treatment in humans.
omissions: Independent replication and human efficacy absent; chronic dosing, infection risk, immunogenicity, cost and IP unknown.
rivalHypotheses: Selectivity may depend on receptor abundance and inflammatory state.
Durability may partly reflect exposure rather than geometry.
whatChanged: New primary preclinical paper with source data and a receptor-geometry approach to separate myeloid suppression from T-cell stimulation.
whyNow: Version of record published 2026-10-14; no prior candidate for this result found in checked bundles.
whatItEnables: Testable strategy for cell-selective cytokine receptor agonism.
readiness: Preclinical animal models; no human efficacy established.
constraints: Biologic manufacturing and clinical development dominate feasibility; no commercial cost data.
crossDomainOpportunity: Open analysis of receptor density, pSTAT3 dose-response and cell selectivity; no paid opening verified.
nextBoundedMachineMove: Reproduce source-data plots; audit dose-response, donor selectivity, receptor density and NHP tables.
